'''Nathalie Deruelle''' (born 1952){{r|born}} is a French physicist specializing in [[general relativity]] and known for her research on the [[two-body problem in general relativity]] and on [[cosmological perturbation theory]].{{r|isgrg}}

==Education and career==
Deruelle began her studies at the [[École normale supérieure (Paris)|École normale supérieure]] in 1971, earned an [[agrégation]] in 1975, then, after visiting positions at the [[European Space Agency]] and the [[University of Cambridge]], completed a doctorate in 1982 at [[Pierre and Marie Curie University]].{{r|lemonde}}

Formerly a director of research for the [[French National Centre for Scientific Research]], associated with [[Paris Diderot University]],{{r|abio}} she is now listed as a researcher emeritus.{{r|apc}}

==Books==
Deruelle is the author of books including:
*''Relativity in Modern Physics'' (with Jean-Philippe Uzan, 2018){{r|cern}} (translated by Patricia de Forcrand-Millard) {{isbn|0198786395}} {{LCCN|2018933841}}
*''Les ondes gravitationnelles'' (with Jean-Pierre Lasota, 2018) {{isbn|2738143342}}
*''De Pythagore à Einstein, tout est nombre : la relativité générale, 25 siècles d'histoire'' (2015) {{isbn|2701195012}}
*''Théories de la relativité'' (with Jean-Philippe Uzan, 2014) {{cite book|title=Seconde édition. Revue et augmentée|year=2019|isbn=979-1035807016|postscript=; 704 pages, pbk |last1=Deruelle |first1=Nathalie |last2=Uzan |first2=Jean-Philippe |publisher=Belin }}

==Recognition==
Deruelle was named a Fellow of the [[International Society on General Relativity and Gravitation]] in 2013 "for her contributions to the two-body problem in general relativity and to relativistic cosmology".{{r|isgrg}}
